title: AgenticVideoToolSchemas
description: Canonical JSON contract for the tools exposed by src.executor.mcp_server.

probe_video.name: probe_video
probe_video.description: Extract container and stream metadata including duration, resolution, frame rate, codecs, and audio channel presence.

source.description: Local filesystem path or accessible URI to video file.

transcribe.name: transcribe
transcribe.description: Transcribe spoken audio from the video into time-aligned segments using Whisper.

source.description: Video or audio file path.

model_size.description: Whisper model size for transcription accuracy vs speed tradeoff.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. 'en', 'es') or 'auto' for auto-detection.

vad_filter.description: Apply Voice Activity Detection filter to exclude background noise and silence.

word_timestamps.description: Return precise timestamp for each word in segments.

search_transcript.name: search_transcript
search_transcript.description: Perform lexical or semantic search on video transcripts to find temporal moments corresponding to queries.

source.description: Video source path.

query.description: Search text or topic to find in speech transcript.

top_k.description: Maximum number of matched segments to return.

sample_frames.name: sample_frames
sample_frames.description: Sample video frames at uniform intervals or target count, returning file paths with exact timestamps.

source.description: Video source path.

end.description: End timestamp in seconds (default: video duration).

count.description: Total frames evenly spaced across interval (overrides fps if specified).

width.description: Thumbnail width in pixels preserving aspect ratio.

output_format.description: Disk paths ('path'), base64 strings ('base64'), or Executor ToolFile ('tool_file').

inspect_window.name: inspect_window
inspect_window.description: Densely sample frames within a narrow temporal window (e.g. 1-15s) for fine-grained action or visual inspection.

source.description: Video source path.

end.description: Window end timestamp in seconds (max recommended 30s).

include_motion.description: Compute optical flow / motion delta score for each frame.

build_visual_index.name: build_visual_index
build_visual_index.description: Start or poll background construction of the local visual frame index. Repeat calls to check progress; frames are processed in bounded chunks.

source.description: Local filesystem path to video file.

search_visual.name: search_visual
search_visual.description: Find when a visible object, person, action, or scene appears. Build the local visual index first if needed, then repeat the same query to poll. Returns ranked hits, merged intervals (the one holding rank 1 is at least 15 seconds long, or the whole searched range when that is shorter; a shorter one is widened evenly around its middle and kept inside the searched range; intervals that overlap it are merged into it), and a contact sheet for visual verification. It matches meaning, not letters, so it cannot find on-screen words or numbers (names, scores, jersey or bib numbers): find those with count_occurrences `text`, which reads text in frames, one window of up to 2400 s per call.

start_sec.description: Seconds, or a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Seconds, or a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

outputSchema.description: Search status or ranked hits, merged intervals, and optional contact sheet.

contact_sheet.name: contact_sheet
contact_sheet.description: Render a composite grid image (contact sheet) with burned-in timestamps for rapid visual timeline scanning in a single image.

source.description: Video source path.

end.description: End timestamp in seconds (default: video duration).

samples.description: Total thumbnail tiles in contact sheet.

cols.description: Number of columns in tile grid.

tile_width.description: Width of each tile thumbnail in pixels.

show_timestamps.description: Render timestamp text badge on each thumbnail tile.

get_clip.name: get_clip
get_clip.description: Extract a temporal video subclip between start and end timestamps.

source.description: Video source path.

re_encode.description: If false, performs fast stream copy on keyframes; if true, re-encodes for frame-exact trimming.

count_repetitions.name: count_repetitions
count_repetitions.description: Count completed cycles of a repeated visual action (jumps, claps, bounces, swings) inside one window of at most 180 seconds. Give `region` (fractions of the frame: x, y, w, h) to isolate the moving thing. Repeat the same call while status=in_progress; verify peak badges and ambiguous edges with inspect_window. For separate appearances of a specific symbol or exact on-screen text use count_occurrences; to locate one moment use search_visual. For a longer clip call once per window, cutting at pauses between cycles so none straddles an edge. The count is a rough first pass and can be far off on real footage. Before answering, count cycles by eye with inspect_window or contact_sheet over the window; if your count differs, trust your own.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

start_sec.description: Start of the window in seconds (default 0). The window may be at most 180 s long. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: End of the window in seconds; defaults to the end of the video. Give both bounds for a video longer than 180 s. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

region.description: Rectangle that contains the repeating motion, as fractions of the frame: x, y (top-left) and w, h (size), with x+w <= 1 and y+h <= 1. Uses w/h; width/height with the same meaning is also accepted. Omit for the whole frame.

fps.description: Sampling rate, default 10. Larger values than 15 are clamped to 15 and the result says so.

method.description: auto (default) picks between motion, embedding and a periodicity check; motion or embedding forces that amplitude counter alone.

min_period_sec.description: Shortest expected cycle in seconds (default 0.4). Bounds the amplitude counter only; the periodicity check ignores it and searches from 0.25 s. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

max_period_sec.description: Longest expected cycle in seconds (default 3); must exceed min_period_sec. Bounds the amplitude counter only; the periodicity check ignores it. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

action_hint.description: Short phrase naming the action being counted, e.g. 'jumping jacks'.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

count_occurrences.name: count_occurrences
count_occurrences.description: Count how many separate times a specific symbol/object or exact on-screen text appears. Use for questions like 'how many separate times does the yellow outlined circle appear (ignore other colours)', 'how many times does the exact word RELEASE appear (not RELEASED)', 'how many times does the green diamond cross the screen'. Give `description` (colour and shape words are enforced, so look-alikes in another colour or shape do not count) and/or `text` (whole-word match by offline OCR). Returns `count` plus one span per continuous appearance (start_sec, end_sec, representative_sec, region, travel, weak); gaps of min_gap_sec or more separate spans. Verify a span with inspect_window at its representative_sec. Not for periodic reps or cycles (use count_repetitions) and not for locating one moment (use search_visual, which ranks frames, is capped at top_k 20 and cannot count). No visual index needed. Repeat the same call while status=in_progress. Lists at most max_spans spans (default 20, maximum 100; larger values are clamped and the result says so); `count` includes any omitted. If 100 or more spans match, the description is too broad: `count` is null, `capped` is true and `spans_found` says how many matched, so narrow the description or window and rerun instead of reporting a number. A min_gap_sec above 0.3 can join separate appearances; then `gaps_merged` and `count_without_merges` are set. The count is a rough first pass: it can merge separate appearances that are split by a scene cut, split one appearance into many spans, and count appearances rather than crossings. The result also carries `contact_sheet`, one labeled image with a tile per listed span (the first 24), in span order: a zoomed frame of that span's best detection with the match boxed, labeled like '#2 29.9s'. Before answering, look at each tile and drop any span whose tile is not the asked-for thing; a span with `weak: true` (one detection, a very short span, or a low score; its label ends in *) is likelier false but is still included in `count`. The answer is the number of tiles that match, plus any spans without a tile, and it must respect `capped`, `gaps_merged` and `count_without_merges` above; if your own count by eye differs, trust yours.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

description.description: Visible thing to count, e.g. 'yellow outlined circle', 'green diamond', 'red star'. Name its colour and shape; text on screen goes in `text`.

text.description: Exact on-screen phrase, matched as whole words (RELEASE matches 'RELEASE' and 'RELEASE NOTES', not 'RELEASED' or 'PRE-RELEASE').

case_sensitive.description: Require the same letter case for `text`.

start_sec.description: Seconds, or a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Defaults to the end of the video. At most 2400 frames are analyzed per call, so fps is lowered automatically on long windows. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

fps.description: Sampling rate, default 5. Appearances shorter than 1/fps can be missed; raise it for brief flashes. Larger values than 15 are clamped to 15 and the result says so.

min_gap_sec.description: Absence of at least this long starts a new span; shorter dropouts stay inside one span. Raising it above the default 0.3 JOINS separate appearances whose gap is shorter than it (0.8 merges appearances 0.7 s apart); the result reports gaps_merged and count_without_merges when that happens. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

max_spans.description: Maximum spans listed (default 20, maximum 100; larger values are clamped to 100 and the result says so). `count` always includes every span.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

count.description: Number of separate appearances; null when capped is true.

capped.description: True when 100 or more spans matched: the description is too broad and count is null.

spans_found.description: How many spans matched; only set when capped.

gaps_merged.description: Appearance pairs joined because min_gap_sec is above the default 0.3; only set when it joined some.

count_without_merges.description: The count if those joined pairs were kept apart.

travel_counts.description: Net motion of appearances across the frame, by direction (left_to_right, right_to_left, top_to_bottom, bottom_to_top); only set when some move. Each value is an estimate from a span's first and last positions, not a verified crossing or direction count. The count includes every direction; directional counting is unsupported, so verify any directional answer visually (inspect_window) before reporting it.

travel.description: Estimated net motion of the match from its first and last positions in the span, not a verified crossing. Verify directional questions visually.

weak.description: True for a single detection, a span shorter than 0.5 s, or a score below 75% of the median span score. Weak spans are still counted; their tile label ends in *.

contact_sheet.description: One image (file_path, tool_file) with a labeled tile per listed span, in span order, up to 24: a zoomed frame of the span's best detection with the match boxed. `labels` lists the tile labels, e.g. '#2* 29.9s' (* = weak).

probe_video.name: probe_video
probe_video.description: Read a video's duration, frame rate, resolution, codecs, and whether it has an audio track and a video track. Call this first: duration_sec bounds every start_sec/end_sec you pass to other tools. Audio-only files (.m4a, .mp3, .wav) are accepted: has_video is false and width, height and fps are 0. has_audio tells you whether transcribe, search_transcript and the audio tools (audio_onsets, loudness_timeline, spectrogram_window) can work; the visual tools and sync_check need has_video true. `source` is a local file path or a video URL and is the same in every tool: an x.com / Twitter post with a video, a YouTube link, another site yt-dlp supports, or a direct .mp4 link. A URL is downloaded once (up to 1080p) and cached; the result gives source_url and local_path, and while the download runs it is status=in_progress, so call again.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

has_video.description: False for audio-only files: width, height and fps are 0, and the visual tools refuse the file.

transcribe.name: transcribe
transcribe.description: Get the full speech transcript as timestamped segments (cached after the first run). Audio-only files (.m4a, .mp3, .wav) work too. To find where a specific word or phrase is spoken, use search_transcript instead of reading it all. If the requested model is not cached, returns another cached transcript with cached_model_size and requested_model_cached=false while one background job runs; with no transcript cached, returns status=in_progress and retry_after_seconds, so repeat the same call after that delay. model_size: tiny, base or small (more accurate, slower on the CPU), or turbo (Whisper large-v3-turbo on the GPU via whisper.cpp: the most accurate and, where installed, the fastest, about 1 minute per hour of audio). Omit model_size to get turbo where it is installed, else tiny. Long audio is decoded in 60-second chunks. Lines repeated 3 or more times in a row carry `suspect` and `notice` names them: speech models often invent such lines over music or silence, though a real chant can repeat too. A line without `suspect` is not verified.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

suspect.description: Only on a flagged line: why it may be invented (the same line 3 or more times in a row). A line without it is not verified.

model_substitution.description: Only when the requested model is not installed: names the installed model used instead.

transcript_path.description: Only when the transcript was too long to list in full: path of a JSON file with every segment.

segments_omitted.description: Only with transcript_path: how many segments are left out of `segments`.

elapsed_sec.description: While status=in_progress: seconds since the background transcription started.

estimated_total_sec.description: While status=in_progress: rough estimate of the whole run, from the audio length and model speed.

estimated_percent.description: While status=in_progress: elapsed / estimated total, capped at 99. An estimate, not a measurement.

search_transcript.name: search_transcript
search_transcript.description: Find when a word or phrase is SPOKEN. Audio-only files (.m4a, .mp3, .wav) work too. Default mode=hybrid lists exact keyword matches first (match=exact: the phrase; match=all_terms: every content word in one segment), then passages that match by meaning (match=semantic: a 20 s window, found on this Mac with EmbeddingGemma 2; nothing is sent to the cloud), so a reworded question still finds the moment. mode=lexical gives keyword matches only. When no hit is exact or all_terms, the words were not found in the speech: semantic hits are the closest passages, not proof, so read their text before answering. If semantic search is not set up or not ready, hits are keyword-only and `note` says why. Returns up to top_k timestamped hits (default 5, maximum 50; larger values are clamped and the result says so; `note` says when more keyword matches exist). For text shown on screen use count_occurrences, and for visible things use search_visual. If ASR is needed, starts or joins background transcription and returns status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds instead of waiting; repeat the same call after that delay. A hit on a flagged line carries `suspect` (see transcribe).

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

query.description: Words or a phrase to find in the speech, e.g. 'launch date'. Punctuation and case are ignored.

top_k.description: Maximum hits (default 5, maximum 50; larger values are clamped to 50 and the result says so).

mode.description: hybrid (default): keyword matches first, then matches by meaning. lexical: keyword matches only.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

top_k_clamped_from.description: The value you requested for top_k before it was lowered to its cap.

suspect.description: Only when the matched line is flagged; see transcribe.

match.description: Why the hit was returned: exact = the query as typed is in the line; all_terms = every content word is in the line; semantic = close in meaning only, so read its text before relying on it.

model_substitution.description: Only when the requested model is not installed: names the installed model used instead.

elapsed_sec.description: While status=in_progress: seconds since the background transcription started.

estimated_total_sec.description: While status=in_progress: rough estimate of the whole run, from the audio length and model speed.

estimated_percent.description: While status=in_progress: elapsed / estimated total, capped at 99. An estimate, not a measurement.

build_visual_index.name: build_visual_index
build_visual_index.description: Start or poll construction of the local visual frame index that search_visual needs. Call it once, then repeat the same call (or search_visual, which reports status=index_required or partial) until the status is complete; frames are processed in bounded chunks. count_occurrences, contact_sheet and the inspect tools do not need the index.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

search_visual.name: search_visual
search_visual.description: Find WHEN something visible happens: an object, person, action or scene (semantic match between the query and sampled frames). It matches meaning, not letters, so it cannot find on-screen words or numbers (names, scores, jersey or bib numbers): find those with count_occurrences `text`, which reads text in frames, one window of up to 2400 s per call. Returns up to top_k ranked frame hits (default 5, maximum 20; larger values are clamped and the result says so), merged intervals (the one holding rank 1 is at least 15 seconds long, or the whole searched range when that is shorter; a shorter one is widened evenly around its middle and kept inside the searched range; intervals that overlap it are merged into it), and a contact sheet to verify them. It ranks frames, so it cannot count: to count separate appearances of a symbol or exact on-screen text use count_occurrences, for a repeated action use count_repetitions, for spoken words use search_transcript. Build the local visual index first (build_visual_index), then repeat the same query to poll until complete. Use start_sec/end_sec to search one range at a time.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

top_k.description: Maximum frame hits (default 5, maximum 20; larger values are clamped to 20 and the result says so). This ranks frames and cannot count: use count_occurrences for counts.

start_sec.description: Inclusive start of the range to search, in seconds. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Exclusive end of the range to search, in seconds; defaults to the end of the video. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

outputSchema.description: Search status or ranked hits, merged intervals, and optional contact sheet.

contact_sheet.name: contact_sheet
contact_sheet.description: Get ONE grid image of evenly spaced frames, with burned timestamp badges, across the whole video or a start_sec/end_sec range: the cheapest way to see what a video contains before searching. Default 12 samples, at most 150 (larger values are clamped and the result says so). Use it to survey; use search_visual to find a specific thing, overview_chunks to survey a long video as ordered sheets, and inspect_window or inspect_windows for dense consecutive frames of a short span.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

samples.description: Requested number of thumbnails; values above 150 are accepted and clamped to 150.

start_sec.description: Optional inclusive start of the overview range in absolute video seconds. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Optional exclusive end of the overview range in absolute video seconds. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

review_video.name: review_video
review_video.description: First look at a video in ONE call: container metadata (duration, size, fps, codecs, has_audio), a contact sheet image with burned timestamp badges (default 24 samples; `samples` up to 150, larger values are clamped and the result says so), every cut and transition from detect_cuts, and a loudness summary (average and peak level, silence gaps, the strongest band-energy outliers with their times). It runs probe_video, contact_sheet, detect_cuts and loudness_timeline for you, so start here instead of calling them one by one. Finishes in a few seconds on clips up to about 10 minutes. `loudness` is null when the video has no audio track. Use the times it returns to zoom in with inspect_window or spectrogram_window; for a different threshold, window or time range call detect_cuts or loudness_timeline directly. Any step failing fails the whole call with that step's error message.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

samples.description: Contact sheet thumbnails (default 24; values above 150 are clamped to 150 and the result says so).

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

metadata.description: Same fields as probe_video: source_path, duration_sec, width, height, fps, format_name, size_bytes, has_audio, has_video, audio_codec, video_codec, fingerprint.

contact_sheet.description: Same fields as contact_sheet: file_path, sample_count, rows, cols, start_sec, end_sec, timestamps, frame_width, frame_height, tool_file (the image), and samples_clamped_from when samples was lowered.

timestamp_sec.description: Time of the change in seconds. For a cut this is the first frame of the new shot; for a transition it is the middle.

score.description: Detector strength 0-1. Not comparable between kinds. A cut between two similar pictures can score below the threshold.

kind.description: "cut" for a hard cut, "transition" for an animated change (fade, dissolve, slide, wipe, zoom).

cuts_total.description: How many cuts and transitions were found in all.

cuts_omitted.description: How many cuts entries were left out of the list.

loudness.description: Null when the video has no audio track.

average_rms_dbfs.description: Energy-averaged RMS level over the whole video, in dBFS.

peak_dbfs.description: Loudest sample on any channel, in dBFS.

window_sec.description: Window length the outliers were measured in.

silence_gaps.description: At most 20 silent stretches, in time order.

fault_outliers_total.description: How many outliers are fault level (not informational).

outliers.description: At most 10: fault-level first, then the largest delta_db. Call loudness_timeline for the full list.

overview_chunks.name: overview_chunks
overview_chunks.description: Survey a long video as consecutive contact sheets, one per chunk_sec (default 60 s), so every stretch is covered in order. At most max_chunks sheets per call (default and maximum 32): for a longer video raise chunk_sec or page through it with start_sec/end_sec; a call over budget fails and says what chunk_sec would fit. samples_per_chunk defaults to 8 (maximum 150, larger values are clamped). Use contact_sheet instead when one sheet is enough.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

chunk_sec.description: Seconds covered by each sheet (default 60, maximum 600). Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

samples_per_chunk.description: Thumbnails per sheet (default 8; values above 150 are clamped to 150 and the result says so).

start_sec.description: Optional inclusive start in absolute video seconds. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Optional exclusive end in absolute video seconds; defaults to the end of the video. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

max_chunks.description: Most sheets in one call (default and maximum 32; larger values are clamped). The call fails if the range needs more chunks: raise chunk_sec or narrow the range.

source_url.description: The video URL you passed as `source`; only present when `source` was a URL.

local_path.description: Cached local copy of `source_url`; pass it to other tools or ffmpeg to skip the URL lookup.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

samples_per_chunk_clamped_from.description: The value you requested for samples_per_chunk before it was lowered to its cap.

max_chunks_clamped_from.description: The value you requested for max_chunks before it was lowered to its cap.

refine_temporal_beam.name: refine_temporal_beam
refine_temporal_beam.description: Zoom into candidate time windows: splits each window into `fanout` contiguous child ranges and returns one timestamped contact sheet per child, without ranking relevance. Use it after contact_sheet or search_visual has narrowed the answer to a few windows and you want to localize inside them; use inspect_windows for dense consecutive frames instead. Budget: windows x fanout x samples_per_child must be at most max_total_samples (default 96, maximum 300); a call over budget fails and says which of the three to lower.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

start_sec.description: Seconds, or a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: Seconds, or a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

windows.description: Absolute time ranges to zoom into, e.g. [{"start_sec": 10, "end_sec": 40}], each within the video.

fanout.description: Child ranges per window (default 4, maximum 8; larger values are clamped and the result says so).

samples_per_child.description: Thumbnails per child range (default 3, maximum 12; larger values are clamped and the result says so).

context_sec.description: Seconds of padding added to each side of every window (default 0). Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

detect_cuts.name: detect_cuts
detect_cuts.description: List scene changes (timestamp_sec, score, kind) in the whole video or a start_sec/end_sec range. Hard cuts and animated changes (fades, dissolves, slides, wipes, zooms) are both returned; `kind` tells them apart: "cut" or "transition". A transition's timestamp is its middle. Scores of the two kinds are not comparable. threshold 0-1 (default 0.25) applies to hard cuts only: raise it to keep only stronger cuts. A hard cut between two similar pictures is found by a second check and listed as a cut with a score below the default threshold; any threshold above 0.25 leaves these out. A change that is over within about 4 frames (a very fast wipe) is listed as a cut, and a few similar-picture cuts still come back as a transition. Film footage with heavy motion can still give false transitions; check a doubtful one with inspect_moments. At most 500 cuts are listed; `total` is the full count and the result says how to see the rest. Use it to segment a video into shots or find edit points; use audio_onsets for sounds and sync_check to compare both.

check_frame_cadence.name: check_frame_cadence
check_frame_cadence.description: Find stretches where the picture updates less often than the file's frame rate, e.g. a 30 fps capture padded to 60 fps so every frame is doubled (judder). It decodes every frame at 160x90 grey and calls a frame a repeat when it is near-identical to the one before; a range is a stretch of at least 0.5 s where repeats fill at least a quarter of every half second while other frames still change. Each range gives start_sec, end_sec, frames, duplicate_frames and effective_fps (unique frames per second; compare with frame_rate). Runs of repeats longer than 0.5 s are holds (still shots, title cards, stalls) and are not ranges; held_frames counts them (use detect_cuts and the frozen-picture check in `python -m src.loop check` for those). It does not judge whether a range is intended: a 24 fps film in a 60 fps file is one range covering the whole file, and a slow, smooth pan can look like repeats. Look at a range with inspect_window to see what moves there. At most 500 ranges are listed; `total` is the full count. Reads the whole file: about 1 s per 700 frames of 1080p; there are no range arguments.

tolerance_ms_clamped_from.description: The value you requested for tolerance_ms before it was lowered to its cap.

cuts_omitted.description: How many cuts entries were left out of the list.

unmatched_strong_onsets_omitted.description: How many unmatched_strong_onsets entries were left out of the list.

search_window_ms.description: The window used to pair cues with onsets, in ms.

bpm.description: The tempo passed in, or null.

beats_per_bar.description: Beats per bar used with bpm; null without bpm.

profile.description: Mean level per third-octave band name.

cue_signatures.description: Learned sound signature for each cue group, keyed by group name.

band.description: The band measured: 'broadband' or a 'low-high Hz' range.

also_matches.description: Other cue groups that sound at this same moment.

uncued_sounds.description: Strong sounds with no cue, found from a cue group's repeated sound.

label_sounds.name: label_sounds
label_sounds.description: Name the sounds in a stretch of a video's audio: cuts [start_sec, end_sec] (both required) into windows of window_sec (default 5 s, at most 60 windows per call) and returns, per window, the chance of each label plus none_chance, from a cloud model (Clef-omni on Cloudflare Workers AI). THIS SENDS THE AUDIO TO CLOUDFLARE: never use it on personal recordings. The server needs CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (or AGENTIC_VIDEO_CF_TOKEN_COMMAND, a command that prints the token) and the call fails with a message naming what is missing. `labels` (default: 20 common sounds such as dog barking, siren, glass breaking, church bells) is the closed list to choose from, so a sound outside the list is forced onto the nearest label or none: list every sound that may be present. Steady musical chords can be named church bells, so treat top_chance under 0.5 as weak and check a hit with spectrogram_window. top_label is null when none_chance beats every label. It does not search: find candidate times with audio_onsets or loudness_timeline first, then label those ranges. For speech use transcribe or search_transcript. Needs an audio track. No window starts after about 40 s and the call answers within about 50 s: a longer range returns the windows finished in time with complete=false and next_start_sec to continue from.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

start_sec.description: Start of the range in seconds. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: End of the range in seconds; at least 1 s after start_sec, and the range may hold at most 60 windows. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

labels.description: Sound names to choose from, e.g. ["dog barking", "siren"] (at most 50, distinct). Default: 20 common sounds.

window_sec.description: Length of each labelled window in seconds (default 5, from 1 to 30). The last window may be shorter; a remainder under 1 s is not labelled. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

complete.description: false when the call stopped early (the time limit or a failed window); the windows returned are the finished ones in order.

next_start_sec.description: Where to start the next call so the unfinished windows are covered; null when complete.

watch_for.name: watch_for
watch_for.description: Watch a stretch of a video for yes/no conditions with a cloud model (Clef on Cloudflare Workers AI) and return the moments each one started to hold. One frame every interval_sec (default 5 s, 1 to 600) from [start_sec, end_sec] is asked every condition (1 to 8 yes/no questions about ONE frame, e.g. "Is a person visible?"); a condition wakes at the sample where its chance of yes has been at least cut (default 0.5) on `consecutive` samples in a row (default 2), at most once per cooldown_sec (default 30) per condition. THIS SENDS VIDEO FRAMES TO CLOUDFLARE: never use it on personal recordings. The server needs CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (or AGENTIC_VIDEO_CF_TOKEN_COMMAND, a command that prints the token) and the call fails naming what is missing, before anything is sent. Only the questions you write can wake: a condition nobody asked about is never reported, so list every event you care about. An event must last at least consecutive x interval_sec to be caught (two samples 5 s apart need about 10 s); lower interval_sec or consecutive for shorter ones, which costs more calls. Accuracy on real footage is not yet measured. At most 720 samples per call; the call answers within about 50 s even when Cloudflare is slow: a longer range, or a sample that keeps failing after its retry, returns the finished samples with complete=false and next_start_sec to continue from (the cooldown does not carry over). This is for finding when something starts to be true; to inspect what happened use inspect_window, for scene changes use detect_cuts, and for sounds use audio_onsets. Results are not cached.

source.description: Local video file path, or a video URL (X/Twitter post, YouTube link, other sites yt-dlp supports, direct .mp4 link). A URL is downloaded once and cached; while it downloads the result is status=in_progress with retry_after_seconds, so call again with the same source.

conditions.description: 1 to 8 distinct yes/no questions about one frame, e.g. ["Is a person visible?", "Is a red rectangle visible?"]. Name what to look for; vague questions give vague chances.

start_sec.description: Start of the range in seconds (default 0). Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

end_sec.description: End of the range in seconds (default: the end of the video). Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

interval_sec.description: Seconds between samples (default 5, from 1 to 600). The range may hold at most 720 samples. Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

cut.description: Chance of yes (above 0, up to 1) at which a sample counts as yes (default 0.5).

consecutive.description: Samples in a row that must count as yes before a wake (1 to 5, default 2).

cooldown_sec.description: Seconds after a wake during which the same condition wakes no more (0 to 3600, default 30). Also accepts a timecode string in MM:SS.mmm form, e.g. 00:14.250.

note.description: Plain-English remark about the call: a capped argument, omitted items, or an ignored unknown argument.

scanned_to_sec.description: Time of the last sample looked at.

time_sec.description: Sample that completed the run of yes samples.

first_seen_sec.description: First sample of the unbroken run of yes samples.

next_start_sec.description: Where to continue when complete is false; null when complete.
